title: Anthropologists and Archeologists

claims.text: Australian archaeologists are bound by the Australian Archaeological Association (AAA) Code of Ethics (accountability, equitable partnership with Indigenous peoples, confidentiality, continuity of records), while anthropologists operate under analogous voluntary professional standards. There is no statutory AI regulator for these occupations; AI use in research engages Indigenous data sovereignty (AIATSIS principles) and human research ethics (NHMRC). A 2026 commentary warns GenAI is fuelling pseudoscience that displaces Indigenous knowledge-informed archaeology online, underscoring the need for free, prior and informed consent and CARE data principles.

claims.text: Jobs and Skills Australia's 'Our Gen AI Transition' Capacity Study (August 2025) scores occupations on augmentability and automatability (0-1, ILO-adapted) across 358 occupations; it finds augmentation outweighs automation economy-wide and that knowledge-intensive professional roles at ANZSCO Skill Levels 1-2 show the highest augmentation exposure. This occupation is a professional Skill Level 1 role, placing it in the high-augmentation, low-automation band.

claims.text: Machine-learning and deep-learning methods (CNNs, Mask R-CNN, visual foundation models, LiDAR derivatives) are increasingly used by archaeologists for automated feature detection and classification from satellite, aerial and LiDAR data, presented as complementary tools that save time and resources while enhancing analysis of large landscapes. A 2026 review of 45 studies finds the techniques automate feature detection but require human expertise for validation.
